did_you_know.text: Did you know? Manasseh became king at the age of twelve and reigned in Jerusalem for fifty-five years. His mother was named Hephzibah.
Did you know? Manasseh not only rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had destroyed, but also built altars to Baal, made an Asherah pole, and worshiped the host of heaven.
Did you know? Manasseh built altars inside the Temple, even though the Temple was intended to be the place where the LORD would put his name in Jerusalem.

Did you know? Among the acts attributed to Manasseh were making his son pass through fire, practicing divination and sorcery, and consulting mediums and spiritists. The chapter describes these acts as sins that angered the LORD.
Did you know? The Asherah pole that Manasseh made was placed in the Temple, the place chosen according to Scripture for the name of the LORD and as a reminder of his covenant with David and Solomon.
Did you know? According to the chapter, Manasseh did not sin alone; he also led Judah astray, so that the people did more evil than the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.

Did you know? The prophecy of destruction uses two vivid images: Jerusalem would be measured with the measuring line used for Samaria and the plumb line used for the house of Ahab, and it would be wiped away like a dish that is turned upside down.
Did you know? The chapter emphasizes that Manasseh’s sins also included shedding a great deal of innocent blood, in addition to leading Judah into idolatry and other evil practices.

Did you know? After his death, Manasseh was buried in the garden of his own house, the Garden of Uzza, and it is not said that he was buried in the tombs of the kings of the house of David. His son Amon succeeded him.
Did you know? Amon became king at the age of twenty-two and reigned in Jerusalem for only two years. His mother was Meshullemeth, the daughter of Haruz, from Jotbah.
Did you know? After Amon’s servants conspired against him and killed him in his house, the people of the land killed the conspirators and made his son Josiah king.
